subject: Order Form redline — termination & auto-renew language alignment
body:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Roberts <sam.roberts@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form redline — termination & auto-renew language alignment

Hi Sam —

Thanks for sending the order form back. I attached our clean order form with the current sales redlines (Acme_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). Two items your procurement team flagged that I want to triage with you and loop in Legal on:

1) Auto-renew trigger and cure: your language asks for a 30-day out notice to opt out but we have a 60-day standard window in the MSA. Can you confirm whether you can accept 60 days, or do you need 30 because of internal billing cycles?

2) Termination for convenience (TfC): procurement proposed a TfC right without service-level carveouts. From our side we need a limited TfC that excludes mid-term committed reserved capacity charges and requires a 60-day notice plus pro rata refund.

I can propose a short fallback: allow 90-day TfC with a one-quarter (25%) pro rata early termination fee for reserved tiers, or keep a 60-day TfC but exclude reserved capacity fees. Want Legal to weigh in on which is lower friction.

Can you confirm labels (which line items are reserved vs usage) so we can mark the order form precisely? Copying Karthik (legal) and Marissa (CS/ops) for ops/implementation impact.

Next steps I propose:
- Sam: confirm whether Acme can accept 60-day opt-out or needs 30.
- Naomi/Marissa: create short SOP for execution timing if TfC exercised (data handoff, access revoke, support ramp down).
- Karhtik: quick redline suggestions for TfC/auto-renew language and fallback fee schedule.

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (redline to current order form)

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Account Exec | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Sam Roberts <sam.roberts@acme.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form redline — termination & auto-renew language alignment

Hi Naomi —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear notes. A couple quick clarifications from procurement:

- Opt-out notice: Acme's billing system runs monthly close windows and finance needs a 30-day out in the order form to line up invoicing; 60 days adds friction to our renewals calendar. Can Redwood accept 30 days for the order form?

- TfC scope: We are OK with a carveout for reserved capacity, but procurement asked for a more limited carveout: TfC should not apply to committed minimums for the first 12 months. After 12 months, TfC can apply with a 60-day notice and pro rata credits.

I attached our procurement rollup for internal context (Acme_Procurement_Rollup.pdf). If we can't get 30 days we can escalate, but we would prefer to keep the order evergreen with a 30-day opt-out so our renewal ops works predictably.

Let me know if a one-page amendment that specifies reserved-capacity carveouts and a 30-day opt-out works — we can sign that parallel to the order form.

Regards,
Sam Roberts
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Corporation
sam.roberts@acme.com

-----
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Order Form redline — termination & auto-renew language alignment

Folks — forwarding Sam's reply. Key asks: Acme wants 30-day opt-out and a TfC that doesn't apply to committed minimums in the first 12 months; OK to allow TfC after 12 months with 60 days and pro rata. They proposed a one-page amendment to capture both if we prefer that to reworking the MSA.

Marissa — can you model the revenue/ops impact of: (A) accepting 30-day opt-out with reserved capacity carveouts, vs (B) keeping 60-day opt-out and proposing the amendment approach? Need to know what level of committed revenue risk we can tolerate and whether billing systems can handle a 30-day opt-out.

Karthik — can you draft two compact redline options we can send back:
1) Sales-friendly: 30-day opt-out in order form + carveout language that explicitly preserves reserved-capacity commitments for first 12 months but allows TfC after with 60-day notice and pro rata credit; plus a one-quarter early termination fee if we have to refund reserved provisioning costs.
2) Legal-first: keep 60-day opt-out, but allow Acme a 30-day operational exception limited to pilot accounts (<= $50k ARR) with exec waiver; TfC remains limited and excludes reserved capacity fees.

Target: send back to Acme by EOD Wednesday (5/20) so procurement can circulate internally. I'm trying to avoid escalation to procurement leadership but we should be ready to accept option (1) if revenue risk is within sea level X (TBD by Marissa).

Thanks —
Naomi

-----
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form redline — termination & auto-renew language alignment

Naomi / Marissa —

Thanks for the context. Attached is a compact set of redline suggestions (redline_suggestions.docx) and a 1-page amendment template that implements option (1) if you choose the faster sales path. High-level legal guidance below:

1) Opt-out notice
- We can accept a 30-day opt-out in the order form only if the order form explicitly ties opt-out to invoice cutoff dates and includes an explicit "effective termination date" that is the first day of the month after the 30-day notice period. This prevents mid-cycle billing disputes.

2) Termination for Convenience
- We should not agree to a TfC that gives Acme a full refund of reserved provisioning costs. Proposed compromise:
  - TfC allowed after the first 12 months for committed tiers.
  - For any TfC exercised prior to full completion of the committed period, Acme pays a termination fee equal to the lesser of (a) 25% of the remaining committed fees, or (b) the actual non-recoverable provisioning costs, with Redwood to provide reasonable proof of provisioning costs if requested.

3) Implementation & data handoff
- Add a short schedule (Schedule X) that captures handoff timelines (30 days for data export request, 15 days to revoke access) and responsibilities to avoid operational ambiguity.

4) Amendment vs MSA redline
- One-page amendment is acceptable operationally and reduces risk of MSA divergence across customers. Use amendment to record the 30-day opt-out for this account only and preserve standard MSA language for others. Include an explicit clause that the amendment does not amend the MSA outside the order form unless signed by both parties.

I've kept the redlines tight and annotated comments to reduce back-and-forth. If sales wants to proceed with option (1) we'll send the amendment and the order form redline together; if they prefer legal-first option (2) I'll prepare the MSA redline but that will add another round with Legal Ops.

Attachments: redline_suggestions.docx

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
